newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat near 700 to dlr, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat near 700 to dlr, trade thin.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed in light volume at 698-702 per dollar on the local interbank market, unchanged from 697-704 in the morning after a range-bound trade, dealers said.
"Very thin volumes traded near 700 throughout the day, because both dollar demand and supply were low," said a dealer.
The lev's fall by around 15 from Wednesday's close was due solely to the longer value date of spot deals, another dealer said. The lev closed around 683-685 on Wednesday.
The value date of today's spot deals is Tuesday because banks in the United States will be closed on Monday for Martin Luther King Day, traders said.

The large spread between interest rates of lev- and dollar-denominated deposits allows for a daily dollar rise by 3.0-3.5 levs, dealers said. Central bank main interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was seen buying small dollar volumes near 700 levs in a bid to boost its thin foreign exchange resrves, dealers said. BNB officials were not available for comment.
BNB foreign exchange reserves stood at $518 million at end-December, down from $525 million a month earlier.
Bulgaria has to pay some $135 million Brady bond coupon on January 28 out of a total of $300 million foreign debt payments due in the first quarter.
